detailed_description: The Code Screenshot Generator turns a snippet of code into a styled PNG image in the browser. You paste code into the editor, pick a theme (Dracula, GitHub, or Nord), choose a language label (JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, HTML, CSS, JSON, or Bash), drag sliders to set padding (16-64px) and font size (12-24px), and toggle line numbers and macOS-style window controls. A live preview shows the styled card on a gradient background, and clicking Download PNG renders the card with html2canvas at 2x scale and saves it as a PNG file. The highlighter applies a small set of regex rules for comments, strings, and a JavaScript-style keyword list, so colour accuracy is best for JS/TS-like syntax. The tool does not parse ASTs, use TextMate grammars or WebAssembly, support hundreds of languages or themes, import from GitHub Gist, export SVG, generate Markdown image links, or scale the image beyond a fixed 2x render.
usage_steps: Paste your code into the editor textarea.
Pick a theme (Dracula, GitHub, Nord) and a language label from the dropdowns.
Adjust padding and font size with the sliders, and toggle line numbers and the window controls dots as needed.
Watch the preview update on the right to confirm the look.
Click Download PNG to save the rendered card as a PNG image.
usage_examples: Render a short JavaScript helper function for a tutorial blog post.
Capture a TypeScript type definition with line numbers and the GitHub theme for a doc page.
Save a Bash one-liner with the Nord theme and minimal padding for a slide.
Disable the window controls to produce a flatter card for a Markdown README.
